deities: Lord Shiva (central shrine; the great seated statue on the complex is dedicated to Shiva as Kirateshvar Mahadev)
Lord Shiva as Rameshwaram (replica Rameswaram Dham)
The twelve Dwadash Jyotirlingas in replica shrines encircling the main Shiva statue
Shirdi Sai Baba (separate temple within the complex)

history.summary: The Namchi Char Dham - properly the Siddheshwar Dham (Solophok Chardham) - is a Hindu pilgrimage-cum-cultural centre on Solophok hill, about 5 km from Namchi town, developed by the Sikkim government. It brings replicas of India's four great dhams - Badrinath (north), Dwarka (west), Jagannath Puri (east) and Rameswaram (south) - under one roof, so devotees may gain the merit of the Char Dham yatra in one visit. The complex centres on a great seated statue of Lord Shiva encircled by replicas of the twelve Dwadash Jyotirlingas, with a grand statue of Kirateshvar Mahadev and a Shirdi Sai Baba temple also on the grounds. The pran pratishtha was performed by Jagadguru Shankaracharya Swami Swarupananda Saraswati in the presence of Chief Minister Pawan Chamling. The Dham won the National Tourism Awards 2010-11 for 'Most Innovative/Unique Tourism Project' from the Ministry of Tourism. A Yatri Niwas accommodates over 90 pilgrims. NOTE: the Shiva statue's height is reported as 108 feet by the Government of Sikkim (namchi.nic.in), while several sources describe an 87-ft statue atop a 108-ft main Shiva temple - verify.

name: Namchi Char Dham
town_description: Namchi is the headquarters of Namchi district (South Sikkim), about 78 km from Gangtok, and a major religious-tourism hub of the state with the Char Dham, Samdruptse (Guru Padmasambhava statue) and the Sai Mandir.

travel.airport: Bagdogra Airport, West Bengal, about 102 km from Namchi (per namchi.nic.in); Pakyong Airport near Gangtok is closer by air distance (verify).
travel.railway: New Jalpaiguri (NJP) Station, West Bengal, about 96 km from Namchi.
travel.road: About 92 km from Siliguri; SNT buses and shared/private taxis run regularly from Namchi town; Solophok hill is 5 km from Namchi town on the Melli-Jorethang route.

visitor_information.best_time: March to May and October to December for clear mountain views of Kanchenjunga and the valleys.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 8:00/9:00 AM to 5:00 PM daily in most sources; one source lists 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM - verify before visiting. Entry fee around Rs 50 per adult (verify), camera fee extra.
